chosen_values_F.roof_form: gabled, ridge along X, thatch slab with a turf ridge roll (as HOUSE-002); a hipped roof would be equally possible
chosen_values_F.door: one opening in the long +Z wall, centre x = 3.00 m, clear 0.85 x 1.75 m, no door leaf; width within 0.8-0.9 m set by the SB-023 phase-1 assignment by the manager (2026-11-20) (not the brief: door width unknown, U); height 1.75 m (r001: 1.60 m) is an optional r002 change so that a 1.70 m person does not stoop at the door (F; easy to revert: COMMON.door_height)
chosen_values_F.hearth: on the axis (brief) 7.5 m from the east (+X) end (house 57 pit 243, D-houses-recon.md after Pleinerová and Hrala 1988, PDF pp. 55-56) = (0,0,0), pebble paving ellipse 1.9 x 1.6 m (46 pebbles, Stone material); the paving size is F
chosen_values_F.post_spacing: long-wall posts nominally every 1.50 m, each shifted by a seeded +-0.13 m (spacing 1.24-1.76 m); corner posts fixed
chosen_values_F.partitions: daub panels 0.14 m on posts, up to the tie beams (y 2.2), open above; 1.0 m passage at z 0.2..1.2, clear height 1.85 m under a head panel
chosen_values_F.ridge_post_row: central row of ridge posts: internal posts at x = -4.0, -1.5, 4.0 plus the gable centre posts (F; house 57 has no middle row of posts, see deviations)
chosen_values_F.anchors: all anchor positions are F (placement suggestions)
chosen_values_F.finishes: plain / limewash / pattern as described per model

parts_and_uncertainties.part: tool traces / irregularity: round timber default
parts_and_uncertainties.status: E (Bohemia, soil traces) -> A once applied; R/F look
parts_and_uncertainties.note: house posts and beams are round, unhewn or at most lightly hewn timber with a waney edge kept; the soil traces give nothing on bark or surface (E-house-tool-traces.md sections 2.2, 3 row 'Split versus hewn')

parts_and_uncertainties.part: tool traces / irregularity: axe facets and stop marks on a minority of posts
parts_and_uncertainties.status: A (Must Farm, England); size and count R/F
parts_and_uncertainties.note: 6 posts carry a shallow facet zone with a step (stop mark) at each end; two of them are the door jambs, hewn over their full height on the face toward the opening, and the lintel has one facet on its top; facet size, count and place are our choice (sections 3 'Axe facets', 4)

parts_and_uncertainties.status: R/F (lake-site analogy A for the use of split timber)
parts_and_uncertainties.note: one internal ridge post per house is a D-section post (minority, our choice, not a Bohemian norm; hidden inside the house, visible only with the roof off)

parts_and_uncertainties.part: tool traces / irregularity: taper, slight bend and lean, uneven diameter and cut heights
parts_and_uncertainties.note: selected round timber stays fairly uniform (Must Farm piles 'very regular') but is never a perfect cylinder; the numbers (diameter 16-25 cm, lean up to 5 cm, bow up to 3 cm) are ours

parts_and_uncertainties.part: tool traces / irregularity: uneven post spacing
parts_and_uncertainties.note: wall-post spacing varies by +-0.13 m around the r001 nominal; the sources say 'uneven' without numbers (Must Farm gives 1.2-3.3 m for a round building in England)

parts_and_uncertainties.status: E (Turnov flat bases, soil traces) / A
parts_and_uncertainties.note: posts end with a blunt, slightly uneven butt at or just below the floor line; no pointed posts (pencil points belong to driven stakes only)

parts_and_uncertainties.part: tool traces / irregularity: axe-chopped ends, branch stubs, burls
parts_and_uncertainties.note: ends are cut obliquely, some posts keep one or two short branch stubs or a burl; no source discusses knots (section 3 row 'Knots and branch stubs')

parts_and_uncertainties.part: tool traces / irregularity: lapped plates and ridge beam, withy lashings
parts_and_uncertainties.status: A (simple joints, twisted withies) / X; placement R/F
parts_and_uncertainties.note: wall plates and the ridge beam are two lapped pieces tied with twisted-withy collars with loose ends; rafters are lashed to the ridge beam on part of the pairs; no mortise-and-tenon detail (section 3 rows 'Joints', 'Lashings')
parts_and_uncertainties.source: Must Farm PXA II, 218, 221; Lobisser 2018 (X); Sklenářová 2012, 51, 53, 55

parts_and_uncertainties.status: E for the existence of smoothed, coloured daub and rod impressions; look R/F
parts_and_uncertainties.note: hand-smoothed lumpy daub (thinner than nominal by 0-0.075 m, never thicker), sweeps, hairline cracks, repair patches, eight chipped spots per 16 m strip, each with its own place and shape, with faint rod impressions of uneven pitch; no planed or perfectly flat plaster

parts_and_uncertainties.part: tool traces / irregularity: limewash and pattern finishes
parts_and_uncertainties.status: trial (brief); E for painted plaster, R/F for look
parts_and_uncertainties.note: unchanged in intent: limewash with flaking and cracks; the white geometric frieze is hand-painted (wavering lines, uneven strokes, gaps); where the pattern sat on a house is unknown

eave bundle ends step by 0.25-0.6 m runs (drop up to 0.085 m), thickness varies with a metre-scale field, ridge roll sags and varies in width, 4 fresh repair patches (low ragged mounds whose outline is irregular and whose edge takes the tint of the surrounding thatch), straw tone varies, silvering and moss in the texture; thatch only, as decided

parts_and_uncertainties.part: tool traces / irregularity: weathering and patina
parts_and_uncertainties.note: darker, damper post feet and roof eaves, silvered straw, soot toward the ridge, tone patches in vertex colours

parts_and_uncertainties.part: tool traces / irregularity: no sawn, planed or perfectly regular surfaces
parts_and_uncertainties.note: no plane-smoothed faces (Lobisser: 'we cannot prove that planes were common tools'; leaving them out is our choice), no octagonal posts, no uniform rods or patterns

deviations: Textures embedded as JPEG (core glTF image/jpeg, no extension) instead of PNG to keep each GLB small; the museum re-encodes them as lossy WebP on import.
Three GLBs per type (one per finish) with identical geometry; the timber and thatch images are identical bytes in all six GLBs, but each GLB embeds its own copy (GLB is self-contained).
No .blend saved: the generator is the native source (bpy from PyPI); rerun it to get the scene.

Door clear height 1.75 m (r001: 1.60 m; HOUSE-002 r001: 1.50 m): an optional r002 change (F), so that a 1.70 m PERSON-001 does not stoop at the door; the partition passages are 1.85 m clear (r001: 1.70 m). The thatch eave is now uneven (bundle ends drop by up to 0.085 m): the lowest eave point is measured in checks/spatial_check.json roof.eave_lowest_y.

Vertex colours (COLOR_0) are exported on all meshes (patina, damp at the post feet, tone patches); the museum import keeps them as vertex colours multiplied with the albedo texture. The timber texture is an atlas of three column bands (round surface, hewn facet, lashing) addressed by UV.
Post, rafter and tie-beam positions differ from r001 by seeded jitter (bounds in irregularity_r002.bounds_F); rafter pairs 16 (r001: 18, hidden under the thatch). Anchors are unchanged.
Type A has a 4th material 'Stone' (untextured, base colour only) for the pebble hearth paving, part of the Frame mesh.

Central ridge-post row (internal posts at x = -4.0, -1.5, 4.0 and the gable centre posts) makes the model two-aisled, an F choice that conflicts with the model source: house 57 has no middle row of posts; its east room has only 5 irregularly placed post holes that did not disturb the impression of open space (Pleinerová and Hrala 1988, PDF p. 56). The authors' statement that the house is not three-aisled (two inner rows of posts; except perhaps the unclear west end; PDF p. 169) concerns a different feature and only adds support. Only the Knovíz plan of Praha-Čakovice had a partly preserved middle row of roof-beam posts (Soudsky 1966, via Pleinerová and Hrala 1988, PDF p. 168; D-houses-VERIFICATION.md).

Door in the east (hearth) room at x = 3.0 is an F choice that departs from the source hint: house 57 has doubled posts at the partition and no posts on the north side of the middle room, both read as a possible entrance to the middle room (D-houses-recon.md, PDF pp. 55-56, 167).
West room 3.5 m outer / 3.23 m clear against house 57's 3 x 5.5 m west room (D-houses-recon.md; the brief gives only the 9 m east room and the 15 m total): the partition lines are F.
